values:
NerdQaxe++ 4.8TH/s Bitcoin Solo Miner — Quad BM1370 ASIC | SHA-256

The NerdQaxe++ is a high-efficiency open-source Bitcoin solo miner powered by four Bitmain BM1370 ASIC chips delivering up to 4.8 TH/s on the SHA-256 algorithm. Built on the popular Bitaxe design, this desktop miner is ideal for solo lottery mining, home node hobbyists, and crypto enthusiasts who want a quiet, low-power alternative to industrial rigs. It features a color IPS status display, WiFi monitoring, and a large 92mm cooling fan with heatsink.

Key Specifications

• ASIC Chips: 4x Bitmain BM1370

• Hashrate: Up to 4.8 TH/s

• Algorithm: SHA-256 (Bitcoin / BTC)

• Power Draw: Approx 75-82W typical

• Input Voltage: 12V DC barrel connector

• Display: Color IPS TFT status screen (LILYGO)

• Connectivity: WiFi 2.4GHz, USB-C config

• Cooling: 92mm fan with dual-tower heatsink

•

• Features & Benefits

• Quad BM1370 layout on the NerdQaxe++ boosts hashrate to 4.8 TH/s while staying under 85W

• Built-in color display shows live hashrate, temperature, voltage, RPM and pool data

Open-source AxeOS firmware with browser dashboard for pool setup and monitoring

• Quiet desktop form factor perfect for solo lottery mining and learning ASIC hardware

•

• Condition & What's Included

Brand new, fully assembled and tested NerdQaxe++ miner as shown in photos.

1x NerdQaxe++ 4.8T miner with fan and heatsink

Note: 12V DC power supply not included unless stated
Ships in protective packaging

Compatibility
Mines Bitcoin (BTC) and any SHA-256 coin. Compatible with public pools and solo mining setups including CKPool solo, public-pool.io, and Braiins. Configured via any modern web browser over WiFi. Requires a 12V DC power supply rated 8A or higher.
Ships securely packaged with tracking. See all photos for exact item condition.

required.name: batteries_required
required.title: Batteries Required
required.note: A regulatory declaration about batteries, not a description. Nothing in the draft states it, and a default here is a false declaration to Amazon and to the carrier.

required.name: supplier_declared_dg_hz_regulation
required.title: Dangerous Goods Regulations
required.note: Amazon's dangerous-goods declaration. It governs how the item may be shipped and stored, and it is the seller's legal statement — this app has no basis to make it.

required.name: list_price
required.title: List Price
required.note: Amazon reads list_price as the manufacturer's list price — the struck-through one. This is the draft's asking price, which is the same number only if the item is not discounted. Where it has an RRP, put that here; the price you charge is in purchasable_offer either way.

conditional.name: externally_assigned_product_identifier
conditional.title: External Product ID
conditional.requirementNote: Required unless you supply merchant_suggested_asin instead.
conditional.note: The draft has no UPC, EAN or ISBN. Amazon will not create a new listing without a product identifier unless your account holds a GTIN exemption for the brand. Find the real barcode or apply for the exemption — a made-up one is an account suspension, not a rejected listing.

conditional.name: merchant_suggested_asin
conditional.title: Merchant Suggested ASIN
conditional.requirementNote: Required unless you supply externally_assigned_product_identifier instead.
conditional.note: The ASIN of an existing Amazon catalogue entry. Nothing in an eBay draft is one, and a guessed ASIN attaches this offer to somebody else's product.

optional.name: number_of_items
optional.title: Number of Items
optional.note: How many units are in one package. The draft's quantity is how many are in stock, which is a different number — 20 miners on a shelf are not a 20-pack. Say how many the buyer receives.

optional.name: item_dimensions
optional.title: Item Dimensions
optional.note: The product's own measurements. The draft has the shipping box, which is larger by however much padding went round it, so it cannot stand in for this.

optional.name: item_type_keyword
optional.title: Item Type Keyword
optional.note: Amazon sets this itself; it is not a seller field.
